title: 40 random dots. Any crowded squares?
hook: Scatter 40 dots over 100 squares at random. Will every square stay almost empty?

knows: random means no pattern, in their head: evenly spread
doesNotKnow: how often pure chance makes lumps

misconception: If dots land at random, no spot gets more than a couple; a cluster means something is attracting them.
objective: The learner can say that about half of random scatters of 40 dots on 100 squares have a square with 3 or more, so lumps alone are not evidence of a cause.
keyState: At least 11 seeded batches dropped, with about half having a ringed (3 or more dots) square; on the click path 60 of 111.

claims.text: Each dot lands at a uniformly random place on the grid, independently of the others.
claims.source: Stage text and model.ts batch(): two mulberry32 uniform draws per dot.

claims.text: The chance that some square among 100 holds 3 or more of 40 random dots is 55.5%.
claims.source: Exact count of placements with every square holding at most 2 dots, via the polynomial (1 + x + x^2/2)^100: P = 1 - 40! [x^40](...) / 100^40 = 0.5550 (pCrowded() in model.ts; recomputed in node).

claims.text: With 25 dots the chance is 18.2%, and with 30 dots 29.3%.
claims.source: pCrowded(25) = 0.1823, pCrowded(30) = 0.2931 (same method). Not shown on the stage; recorded for checking the brief.

claims.text: The tally of batches with a ringed square is a seeded run of batches, shown on the stage as k of m; it varies around the exact 55.5%.
claims.source: Batch i uses mulberry32(9000 + i), untuned. The first 111 batches give 60 of 111 (54%). Over 300 other seed sets of 111 batches the count averaged 61.4 (55.3%) with SD 5.0 (range 47 to 74), so it is near 55% but not equal to it.

claims.text: An evenly spread pattern of dots is the unusual outcome; lumps are what random scatter looks like.
claims.source: Follows from claim 2: more than half of random scatters contain a crowded square. No claim is made about real-world clusters.

recall.question: 30 raindrops land at random on 100 paving stones. Is it surprising if one stone catches 3 or more?
options: No, it happens in roughly 3 scatters out of 10
recall.why: For 30 random drops on 100 stones the chance that some stone gets 3 or more is about 29%. Lumps are ordinary.
